task.title: Make the board usable on a phone-sized screen
task.description:
Workbook has no phone app and this story does not add one. Once a board can be hosted, as "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" describes, a phone reaches it by opening the same address in its own browser. What is missing is a board that works at that size.

The use case is the time away from the desk: check what is next, read a task, capture an idea as a new task, move something along. The same layout serves anyone who opens a local board in a narrow window.

Earlier versions of this story described a standalone app holding Git credentials, then a native client of a hosted server. Both were dropped. There is also no wrapper app around the board: some sign-in providers refuse to sign people in inside an app's embedded browser, and the phone's own browser has no such problem. The earlier texts are in this task's history.

## What does not fit a phone today

- Columns sit side by side, so a board with five statuses is several screens wide.
- On the board, a card moves between columns by being dragged, which is awkward by touch and competes with scrolling.
- The task detail and new-task forms, the header, and the history view were laid out with room to spare.
- The status, priority and key settings panels are dense. They are left as they are in this version.

## Constraints

- One board, one set of pages. This is a layout that adapts, not a second site for phones.
- The board at desktop widths, and inside Workbench, looks and behaves as it does now.
- Nothing here depends on hosting to be useful, but it is scheduled after it because that is when a phone can first reach a board that stays up.

## Decisions

Decided 2026-11-21 unless marked otherwise.

1. A narrow screen shows one column at a time. A row of status names with task counts sits under the header and stays in place while the cards scroll; tapping a status switches to it and slides the row so the chosen one is in view. Dylan approved a mockup of this on 2026-11-21. Swiping sideways between columns is left out of this version, because it competes with scrolling the status row and with the browser's back gesture. The board opens on the status `workbook next` draws from, and after that on the last status viewed on that phone.
2. On a phone-sized screen a task's status is changed from the task's own page, which already has that control. Dragging cards is turned off at that width so it does not compete with scrolling.
3. The first version covers the board, task detail, new task, comments and history. Status, priority and key settings stay out of the phone layout for now (decided 2026-11-18).
4. The board gains an icon and a name so a shortcut saved to a phone's home screen looks right. It is not set up to open as its own app window: a shortcut that opens outside the browser keeps a separate sign-in, the same problem that ruled out a wrapper app.

## Done when

- On a phone-sized screen, in the phone's own browser, a person can see the board, read a task, create one, change status, priority and labels, assign it to themselves, and comment.
- No page needs sideways scrolling to be used, and every control can be hit with a thumb.
- A task's status can be changed by touch without dragging a card.
- This is checked at real phone sizes in a browser, on at least one narrow and one wide phone, not only by reading the page's code.
- The board at desktop widths and inside Workbench is unchanged, and the existing board checks still pass.
- The README says the board works on a phone and how to reach a hosted one from it.
